summary: This small application is the "customer" of the two domain classes: it creates one plain Cookie and one DecoratedCookie, then asks each object to describe itself and prints the answer. It shows that a subclass object is used exactly like its parent, but supplies its own version of the shared behavior.

lines.text: The Cookie class is only a blueprint; new Cookie("Chocolate Chip") is what actually builds an object in memory, and the flavor passed here is stored inside that one object.

A DecoratedCookie is created the same way as a Cookie because the subclass inherits the flavor field and passes the argument up to the parent constructor \u2013 nothing about the flavor had to be written twice.
describe() returns a String rather than printing it, so the application decides what to do with the sentence; here it goes to the console, but the same method could feed a receipt or a web page.
This call looks identical to the previous one, yet the output differs: DecoratedCookie overrides describe(), and Java runs the version belonging to the object's actual class.
